messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Refactored policies
parts:
Hi all,

Just wanted to let you know that I just pushed a refactoring. I touched all our error handling to only use the default.

I spotted some additional problems with our code while refactoring. I left a few notes in the TO-DO.

For Michael, this *shouldn't* affect your refactoring as long as you're relatively up to date with master.

For Peter, for our distributions, we've dropped two signatures, the ones with the Policy template argument. I think this may affect your fvar branch a bit. Let me know how I can help.

I'm out this meeting on Tuesday. Can someone else patch everyone in? I'll be back the following week.


Daniel

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Refactored policies
parts:
Hey,

I found a bug in the new code. It's a subtle one not likely to show
up on some systems, but I've seen it crash things in subtle and hard
to track down ways elsewhere so I thought I'd point it out. Here is
the code from check_pos_definite.hpp

std::ostringstream msg_o;
msg_o << name << error_msg << error_msg2;
T_result tmp =
raise_domain_error<T_result,T_y>(function,msg_o.str().c_str(),y,boost::math::policies::policy<>());

The issue is that msg_o.str().c_str() will produce a pointer to memory
which has been freed. The str() method returns a new, temporary
instance of a std::string. Once c_str() returns, that temporary
instance of the std::string will be destroyed, leaving the pointer
returned by c_str() pointing to a buffer which has just been deleted.

I'm not sure how widespread that pattern is, so I thought I'd email
rather than fix it in one or two places and have it persist elsewhere.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Refactored policies
parts:
I was thinking of changing the type of error_msg passed into dom_err
to be a template parameter. Right now it's a const char* so anyone
using dom_error will have the same issue and will need to create a
temporary string, which makes this error more tempting and therefore
more likely. If you could pass in a std::string, it would be less
likely to happen with people calling dom_err.

In dom_err itself you'll still need to create the temporary
std::string to get the c_str() to pass to raise_domain_error.

Cheers,
Marcus

On Mon, Apr 15, 2013 at 11:30 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
> What do you mean by templating out both error message types?
>
> The first needs to be a char* eventually for boost io formatting. The second is anything that has an insertion operator. I think it's substituted for "%2%", but don't hold me to that.
>
>
> Daniel
>
>

>> Alternatively, you could template out both error message string types.

>> Cheers,

>>>> On Monday, April 15, 2013, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
>>>>>
>>>>> Hey,
>>>>>
>>>>> I found a bug in the new code. It's a subtle one not likely to show
>>>>> up on some systems, but I've seen it crash things in subtle and hard
>>>>> to track down ways elsewhere so I thought I'd point it out. Here is
>>>>> the code from check_pos_definite.hpp
>>>>>
>>>>> std::ostringstream msg_o;
>>>>> msg_o << name << error_msg << error_msg2;
>>>>> T_result tmp =
>>>>>
>>>>> raise_domain_error<T_result,T_y>(function,msg_o.str().c_str(),y,boost::math::policies::policy<>());
>>>>>
>>>>> The issue is that msg_o.str().c_str() will produce a pointer to memory
>>>>> which has been freed. The str() method returns a new, temporary
>>>>> instance of a std::string. Once c_str() returns, that temporary
>>>>> instance of the std::string will be destroyed, leaving the pointer
>>>>> returned by c_str() pointing to a buffer which has just been deleted.
>>>>>
>>>>> I'm not sure how widespread that pattern is, so I thought I'd email
>>>>> rather than fix it in one or two places and have it persist elsewhere.
>>>>>
>>>>> Cheers,
>>>>> Marcus
